errors.evidence: The chart shows data for seven countries and the Eurozone as a whole, not eight countries.
The line for Belgien (Belgium) falls to approximately 85% by 2007, not 90%.
The line for Deutschland (Germany) ends at approximately 60% in 2025, not 65%.
The line for Spanien (Spain) peaks around 2014 at just under 100%, not 105% in 2015.

errors.text_span: (durchgezogene hellblaue Linie mit geringerer Sättigung) beginnt 1995 bei etwa 55 %, steigt bis 2003 auf rund 65 %, fällt bis 2007 auf etwa 60 %, steigt dann bis 2015 auf etwa 95 %, bleibt bis 2020 bei ca. 100 % und fällt bis 2025 auf etwa 105 %
errors.evidence: The description for Frankreich (France) is almost entirely incorrect. It describes a trend (falling between 2003 and 2007) that belongs to Deutschland (Germany). The actual line for France shows a continuous increase from 1995 to a peak over 110% around 2020, and then stays around 110% until 2025.
The line for Italien (Italy) does not remain at 140% until 2020; it rises to a peak of over 150% around 2021.

This phrasing is confusing in context. The description previously stated the value was already at 140% in 2020. The line actually peaks above 150% after 2020 and then falls to 140%, a detail which the description omits, making this statement unclear.
